title: Tissues: What Organs Are Made Of
subject: Biomaterials
summary: Organs combine several tissue types; each tissue is cells plus extracellular matrix plus signalling molecules.

learning_objectives.text: Explain how tissue composition determines how a tissue behaves

concepts.label: Organs combine tissue types
concepts.reference_explanation: Organs are built from several different tissue types working together, such as cartilage, bone and ligament in a knee.
key_points: Organs are built from several different tissue types working together
common_misconceptions: An organ is one uniform material

concepts.label: Four tissue categories
concepts.reference_explanation: There are four tissue categories: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. Cartilage and bone are both connective tissue but have different matrices.
key_points: There are four tissue categories: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous
common_misconceptions: Cartilage and bone are the same tissue

concepts.label: Cells, matrix and signals
concepts.reference_explanation: Tissue is made of cells, extracellular matrix (ECM) and signalling molecules; living cells alone do not make a functional tissue.
key_points: Tissue is made of cells, extracellular matrix and signalling molecules
common_misconceptions: If the cells are alive the tissue is fine
